page: Amazon Web Services c6i.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance in single-core operations but poor multi-core scaling due to the 2-vCPU configuration. The single-core stress-ng CPU test scored 1881.49, and the Geekbench single-core score reached 1622.0, both falling into the average category. However, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core at 1922.07 and Geekbench multi-core at 1856.0 rank in the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read and write speeds of 14.26 GB/sec and 13.09 GB/sec respectively, both ranking in the bottom 10%. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks perform moderately, with gzip compression at 27.86 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 10.26 GB/sec.

The c6i.large offers a compute-focused hardware profile with a low RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2:1. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but have minimal memory footprints. However, the lack of local storage and low baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps present clear bottlenecks for data-intensive applications. Performance in database operations and static web serving is weak to poor. Consequently, this instance is best suited for lightweight compute tasks, single-threaded processing, basic web serving, or utility workloads rather than memory-heavy databases, large-scale software compilation, or multi-threaded data processing.
